support.quote: In 2007, French engineer Pascal Cotte announced that his ultra-high resolution scans of the painting provide evidence that Mona Lisa was originally painted with eyelashes and eyebrows
Cotte discovered that the "Mona Lisa's" eyebrows and eyelashes were originally painted on the piece.
The world's most famous painting originally included both brows and lashes, according to Cotte, who said his 240-megapixel scans reveal traces of Mona Lisa's left brow
but that these had gradually disappeared over time, perhaps as a result of overcleaning
They disappeared either because of a botched attempt to clean the painting or because the paint's oil and pigment faded over time.

assessments.note: Cause given as fading or over-cleaning; the answer 'faded away' matches the card's option C.
